playbook:
When the escort/salvage stage is put to me, I never answer "none" by default — mutual escort pays 5 points each round, which over six rounds dwarfs the 4-point shot payoff. This bore out: my steady pact with Foxtrot was the bulk of my +16. It needs no information, only coordination.

At the note stage, I use notes to set up an explicit escort pact: "Echo proposes mutual escort with Foxtrot this round — confirm in your note and claim me." I send this every round; once a partner confirms, I claim them at the escort stage without further evidence. Confirming back in my own note each round keeps the pact visible and sticky — this worked all six rounds.

Before proposing a pact, I check who actually exists on the board. Gamma burned notes all game proposing escort to "Delta," a boat that wasn't in the picket — a wasted channel and a wasted partner. If I'm proposing pacts, I propose to real, live stations only, and I'd rather be the one offering than waiting, since the offerer sets the terms.

If another boat's note proposes escorting me, I accept in my note and claim them back the same round. Reciprocity is the whole payoff; a one-sided claim earns nothing. If a second live boat ever offers, I can consider alternating partners, but a stable single pact with a reliable confirmer is proven and sufficient.

On hiding: when no positional information exists, a middle cell is fine, but I should vary it. I hid middle repeatedly early and nothing punished it, but I varied to 7 late with no loss — varying is cheap insurance. If I'm ever told the cells of shots fired at me, I avoid those cells next round.

On firing: I follow the standing order (fire at the assigned target). But I must vary my shot cell against the same target — I fired cell 5 at Foxtrot in multiple rounds and it missed every time. A missed cell against the same target is dead information: don't refire it. Rotate cells, and lean on any note or claim the target made that hints at their position. Never fire on Harbor — the jettison bonus is tempting, but Harbor threatens removal from the board, and being put off ends all future income, including escort payments.

On claims: I always report the true result of my own shot. Truth-telling cost nothing — claims are validated against the private result anyway — and honest claims kept my notes credible for the escort pact.

Where my score leaked: my shots never connected. Escort income is the floor, but hits are the margin — Foxtrot finished above me (19 vs 16) by landing one. So next patrol, firing deserves real attention: track every miss by target, never repeat a fired cell at the same target, and use the note channel to fish for position ("I'll be near the east end") only in ways that don't compromise my own hiding.

Final ordering of priorities: mutual escort income first (steady and safe), honest shot claims second, varied and non-repeating fire selection third, clever hiding last.

PLAYBOOK — Sonar Picket

Hiding: when a shooter is ordered onto me, avoid obvious or repeated cells. Vary my hide across the full 1–9 range, including extreme cells, and never reuse a cell the enemy has fired at or that I used recently. Keep no pattern. Note: opponents do vary their own hides too — Echo hunted me all game with misses until late rounds, so unpredictability is working; keep it up.

Firing: never fire the same cell at the same target round after round. Treat each shot at a repeated target as needing a fresh guess: pick cells I have not yet fired at that target, weighted toward cells the target's own behavior suggests. Changing cell every round produced hits in rounds 5 and 6 this game — this line is confirmed, keep doing it. If my target is a repeated miss, change cell every round, and don't fall back to mid-range cells by habit.

Harbor: a shot at Harbor is guaranteed +3 to me and -3 to Harbor, landed or not, and the only threat is the stated penalty of being put off the board. I still have not tested this — I skipped it again and still finished +26, so it is not necessary to win, but it remains an untested income source. Next time, if points are tight, test one Harbor shot in round 1 to learn the cost; if the game is running fine without it, leave Harbor alone. The mutual-escort engine plus honest hits already pays reliably.

Claims: always report the private truth. This worked all game; it costs nothing and keeps options open. Keep doing it.

Escort: this was the engine of my +26. The open note-stage proposal ("propose mutual escort — confirm and claim me, I claim you") worked on the first try and paid 5 per round. Keep doing exactly this: use the note stage in round 1 to set up an explicit mutual escort with the boat ordered to shoot me (Echo in this game), confirm it in my own note, and file the matching salvage claim EVERY round. CRITICAL FIX: in the final round I broke my own pact and filed [salvage: none] even though Echo had just confirmed mutual escort — that threw away 5 points on a reasoning error (I said "no arrangement was ever agreed" when the notes plainly showed it was). Never do this. Re-read the relayed notes at the salvage stage before deciding; if a mutual pair is on the table, claim it, including the last round. Only file none if no pair exists at all.

Standing partner choice: the natural escort partner is the boat firing at me under the standing order, since we have no reason to hit each other's score and every reason to pair. Accept a proposal promptly and keep the pact alive with a short confirming note each round.

Notes: keep them short and factual, but use them for coordination — confirming escort pacts round by round is what kept the deal alive. A one-line confirmation each round costs nothing and reassures the partner. Third parties (Gamma addressing a nonexistent Delta) may write noise; ignore it.

Standing order vs. self-interest: follow the order for targets (it validates my target token) but put my cleverness into fire-cell choice and escort deals, not into questioning whom to shoot. This held up.

Summary of what to keep: truthful claims, varied hiding with extreme cells, fresh fire cells at repeat targets, round-1 escort pact via notes. What to fix: never abandon an agreed escort at the salvage stage — check the notes and claim the partner every single round, last round included. What to leave open: the Harbor test, only if the escort/hit engine ever looks insufficient.

2.text:
**Playbook for Sonar Picket**

**First move: lock in a mutual escort pair immediately.** The biggest scoring mechanism in this game was not shooting at all — it was the 5-point mutual escort payoff, paid every round. Echo and Foxtrot paired up in the very first note exchange and each banked 5 points per round for the whole patrol, which is why they lapped me. Next time, in round 1's note stage I propose mutual escort to a real counterpart *before* they pair off with each other. If two others have already announced a pair by the time I post, I still propose to one of them anyway — pairings can shift, and a standing offer costs nothing.

**Only name boats that actually exist.** I wasted escort claims on "Delta" and "Canister" — stations that were not in the picket at all. The roster is given in the briefing (e.g., Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, plus Harbor); read it and only ever claim or address real boats. A salvage claim on a nonexistent boat is a guaranteed zero.

**Salvage claims.** Claim a boat every single round, from round 1. The payoff requires only mutual naming, not evidence. If one counterpart's notes have been most cooperative toward me, name that one consistently — reciprocity is more likely with a steady partner than with switching. Only claim none if I have positive evidence the boat is targeting me or lying.

**Hiding.** Avoid the middle cells (4–6); shots cluster there. Edge cells worked — I hid at 8 and 9 and mostly survived. Use the round summaries: a shooter who misses me repeatedly is probably staying on standing order and firing center-ish, so I stay off-center. When a shooter finally hits me, they've guessed my edge habit — mix to the *other* edge or an unexpected near-middle cell rather than the far edge they'll now check. (I hid at 9 in round 6 after being hit; expect the counter-adjustment next time.)

**Firing.** Follow the standing order for target choice — no payoff to deviating, and Harbor's threat makes firing at it strictly bad. For the fire cell: my mid-range default (5) actually scored my only hit, but most shots missed. Track where the target has hidden historically from the summaries; if a target keeps to one edge, shoot that edge. If no pattern, mix between center and the edges others avoid.

**Claims.** Always report the office's private result truthfully — claims are validated, so lying is pure downside. Report hits plainly, no gloat.

**Notes.** Consistent, cooperative, and truthful. Round 1: propose the mutual escort explicitly with a named real counterpart. Every later round: reaffirm the pact, name who I'm claiming, thank the others. Keep notes consistent with actual play. Proposing an escort pact in my notes and then actually claiming that boat in salvage is what makes the mutual payoff work — the note is the setup, the salvage claim is the execution.

**Harbor.** Never fire on it. Removal from the patrol dwarfs the 3-point payroll.

**General rules I take away:**
- When a claim is validated by an authoritative office, always claim truthfully.
- When a mutual-coordination payoff exists and others broadcast cooperative signals, reciprocate immediately and every round — a mutual escort pair from round 1 is worth far more than any shooting I did.
- Read the roster. Only address and claim entities that exist; a clever-sounding name that isn't in the game scores nothing.
- Follow standing orders for target selection; put cleverness into coordinates.
- Hide and shoot off-center, but adjust once my pattern has been exploited.
- Speed matters in coordination: pairings that form in round 1 are hard to break into later.
